targetTest: LIVE: the sheet applies the light inside applyLiveConfig, from a getter ref
expected: AquarelleCanvasLayer declares an optional getLight getter prop, mirrors it in a ref, passes it to both applyLiveConfig call sites, and applyLiveConfig reads the getter and calls engine.setLight(light) when present; the mount forwards the getter; the Studio resolves getEfxPaintDocument(layerId)?.light at call time, hands the getter to the canvas mount and the value to all three bake call sites; both store reveal render calls carry light: document.light; the Studio signature carries |${lightSignature(documentLight())}; and lightSignature(undefined) === lightSignature(DEFAULT_LIGHT) === default.
actual: None of the render-path wiring exists yet: the layer has no getLight prop/ref and applyLiveConfig never calls setLight (0/2 getter call sites), the mount has no getAquarelleLight seam, the Studio has no documentLight/documentLight() bake inputs/signature term (0 of 3 light inputs, no lightSignature export in physicsPaintStudioSettings), and neither store render call carries light: document.light (0/2). The file collected and ran 8 tests: 7 fail on their planned pins (LIVE, MOUNT, RESOLVE x2, STORE, SIGNATURE, SIGNATURE BEHAVIOR) and the NO LEAK prohibition guard passes because no payload site carries a light today. The controller suite passed 16/16 including the new two-direction signature row, proving the controller contract is executable even before the Studio emits a light-bearing signature.
semanticAssessment: Both planned shapes failed for the planned reason: every render path still renders with the engine default because nothing reads the document light. Failures are source-pin and export-presence assertions only (no syntax, fixture or load fault): the test file collected, ran, and reported per-row failures. The single passing row is the deliberate prohibition guard (no light in a stroke payload or params bag), which must already hold; the controller row proves the same-signature-twice and changed-signature directions on the existing harness.
